title: Mezzrow, Sammy Price's tour and Paris pay
summary: Mezzrow was well connected but weak on clarinet; Moore later toured with Sammy Price; he earned $400 a week plus expenses.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, both of them together... See, I went over there with Mezzrow, the first one. I went back with Sammy

It was around '55, something like that. Maybe it was before '55... I was working at the Jazz Limited in Chicago, and they let me off to go out to make this tour, said he'd have the job open for me when I came back. I went over with Sammy Price. We made the same, about the same tour -- in Paris, France. But he didn't play the Olympia Theatre. You've got to pull some strings, you've got to know how to get into the Olympia Theatre.
Yeah, you just don't get in there.

You just don't get in there just like that, you know. So Mezzrow, he was a local(?) boy. He spoke the language, he...you know... He'd been all over the place. He wasn't very much of a clarinet player, you know. He had the arthritis in his fingers and his wrists; he couldn't finger so fast. So he played the type of numbers (?) that he was swinging it, which was slow, and he'd play some Blues, you know. So he had (?) numbers like that -- slow.

I got around about... Oh, that was big money there. I got four hundred dollars, room and board. Paid my expenses, hotel, everything, and four hundred dollars. God, that's right around about...oh, that's almost eight hundred dollars altogether.
Yeah, that's okay. Four hundred dollars a week you're talking about..
Yes. Of course, I got half in French money and half...
So I saved the American money up, you know, and I used the French money over there for different things.
